assumptions: The target operating system is Windows, as the user is currently on Windows.
The software will have a Graphical User Interface (GUI) rather than a Command Line Interface (CLI) to make it user-friendly.
Data safety is the highest priority; the tool will not delete any system-critical files or user documents without explicit permission.
candidates: Scanning and cleaning temporary files, log files, and system cache folders.
Scanning and listing large files (e.g. >100MB) for manual user review and deletion.
Finding and listing duplicate files to save disk space.
An interactive visual disk analyzer (e.g. treemap or pie chart) to explore directory usage.
An uninstaller helper to clean up leftover files after removing programs.
confirmed: The user wants to create a software application to clean up and optimize computer disk space.
conflicts: Simple one-click cleaning (for non-technical users) vs. advanced visual disk analyzer (for power users): Attempting to build both for the MVP could bloat the scope and design phase.

gaps.dependency: Defining a strict exclusion list of system directories and active processes.
gaps.impact: Permanent data loss or operating system corruption if critical files are deleted.
gaps.reason: Deleting system files can break the OS if not guarded by a strict whitelist of safe zones or a blacklist of system folders.

gaps.dependency: Defining the target operating system (Windows-only vs. cross-platform).
gaps.impact: Significant codebase changes if cross-platform support is added later without planning.
gaps.reason: Disk APIs, temporary file paths, and registry/system caches are completely OS-specific.

options.impact: Simplifies file scanning, administrative privilege handling, and lets us target Windows-specific paths easily.
options.label: Windows only

options.impact: Requires abstracting all paths and system APIs, using a cross-platform GUI framework, and increases development time.
options.label: Cross-platform (Windows & macOS)

questions.question: Which operating system(s) do you want this software to support?
questions.reason: System APIs and temporary file paths are completely different on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
questions.recommendation_reason: Since your current system is Windows, developing and testing a Windows-only tool is much easier, faster, and allows deeper system integration for the MVP.

options.impact: Focuses on safe, predefined paths (caches, logs, temp). Simple UI and minimal risk of user errors.
options.label: Simple scan and one-click clean

options.impact: Interactive treemaps/pie charts showing disk space distribution, allowing manual selection. Higher risk of user error.
options.label: Advanced visual analyzer and manual selector

questions.question: Who is the primary user and what is the preferred UI/UX style for the MVP?
questions.reason: This determines whether we build a simple 'one-click clean' interface or a complex directory-size visualization tool.
questions.recommendation_reason: It has a lower risk of accidental file deletion, requires less complex UI components, and is faster to develop as a first release.

options.impact: High performance, extremely small executable size, modern web frontend technologies, but requires learning Tauri/Rust structure.
options.label: Tauri (Rust + HTML/JS/CSS)

options.impact: Very fast development speed, standard Python libraries, but results in a larger executable size and potential performance limits.
options.label: Python (PyQt or PySide)

options.impact: Deep native integration with Windows, standard for Windows GUI, but limits easy cross-platform porting in the future.
options.label: C# / .NET (WPF or WinForms)

questions.question: Do you have a preferred technology stack or programming language?
questions.reason: Different frameworks have significant trade-offs in build size, system performance, memory usage, and development speed.
questions.recommendation_reason: Tauri enables building lightweight desktop apps (under 10MB) with web-based UI, running native system scans securely and quickly via Rust.

risks: Accidental deletion of system registry keys or operating system files, rendering the computer unbootable.
Permission errors resulting in crash or incomplete cleanups if the user does not run the program with administrator rights.
Performance issues (high CPU/IO) during deep directory scanning, leading to system freeze or application crashes.
unknowns: The target operating system (Windows only vs. cross-platform).
The primary user profile (average users vs. power users).
The preferred technology stack (Tauri, Python, .NET, etc.).
The exact scope of the MVP features.
